metadata.title: Fictional Company SOC — worked implementation examples — DEMO ONLY
metadata.remarks: Fictional training example selected from NIST SP800-53 Rev. 5.2.0. This is not a NIST Low or Moderate baseline, a complete security requirement set, or evidence of compliance. All ODP values and additional context are illustrative company assumptions.

components.title: Company Security Operations Centre (demo)
components.description: Fictional shared SOC: 24/7 security monitoring, centralized log analysis and incident coordination. Published statements identify implemented sections for an onboarded system; no certification or assurance claim.

control-implementations.description: Statement-by-statement implementation for the fictional seven-control worked example. Only implemented sections are published. Unpublished sections remain the system responsibility, so a control can be partially covered. Evidence is illustrative, not supplied evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: The SOC maintains an event-selection matrix covering authentication, privileged actions, configuration changes and security alerts. During onboarding an analyst generates test events and checks that each arrives in the central log service. The SOC reviews the matrix quarterly and after material changes or incidents, retaining the telemetry register, test results and review decisions as example evidence. System owners enable the source logs, approve exclusions and document the investigation rationale. This is a partial/shared contribution; statement entries identify only implemented sections; all other sections remain system work.

statements.description: The SOC coordinates event selection with incident response, platform operations and audit stakeholders, recording agreed event requirements in the telemetry register.
The SOC reviews and updates the event-selection matrix quarterly and after material changes or incidents, retaining the review decisions.

implemented-requirements.description: SOC analysts review centralized audit records daily and triage high-severity alerts continuously. Saved queries flag repeated authentication failures, unexpected privilege changes, disabled logging and suspicious transfers. Analysts record findings and notify the SOC duty lead and affected system owner; the duty lead increases review coverage when threat intelligence or risk changes. Dated review records, query versions and linked investigation cases are example evidence. System owners maintain log delivery and resolve assigned findings. All published sections are implemented by the SOC for an onboarded system.

statements.description: SOC analysts review centralized audit records daily and triage high-severity alerts continuously. Saved queries detect repeated authentication failures, unexpected privilege changes, disabled logging and suspicious transfers; analysts assess potential impact.
Each SOC daily review records its query period, analyst, findings and linked case IDs. Analysts investigate missing-log alerts as coverage issues even when no threat alert is raised.
SOC analysts report findings to the SOC duty lead and affected system owner through the incident case and duty notification channels.

The SOC duty lead adjusts review frequency, analysis scope and reporting when credible threat intelligence, law-enforcement information or changed risk warrants increased coverage; the decision is recorded in the review log.

implemented-requirements.description: The SOC operates a 24/7 duty rota and severity-based incident playbooks covering preparation, detection, investigation, proposed containment, eradication support and recovery verification. The incident manager coordinates recovery with continuity staff and records decisions in the case timeline. Post-incident reviews produce assigned improvements to playbooks, training and exercises; a common severity matrix and case checklist make handling consistent. Playbooks, case timelines and lessons-learned actions are example evidence. System owners authorize disruptive containment, remove the cause and restore services. This is a partial/shared contribution; statement entries identify only implemented sections; all other sections remain system work.

statements.description: The SOC incident manager coordinates incident handling with business continuity staff and records recovery dependencies and agreed actions in the case timeline.

The SOC uses a common severity matrix, case checklist, escalation timetable and closure review across onboarded systems to make the rigor, scope and results of incident handling comparable and predictable.

implemented-requirements.description: The SOC creates a uniquely numbered case for each reported incident and records affected assets, severity, discovery time, evidence references, actions, owner and current status. Analysts update the timeline at each handover and the incident manager reviews open cases daily until closure. Case histories and closure reviews are example evidence. System owners supply impact and remediation updates, and the incident manager approves closure. All published sections are implemented by the SOC for an onboarded system.

statements.description: The SOC tracks every reported incident in a uniquely numbered case, documenting affected assets, severity, discovery time, evidence references, actions, owner and status. Analysts update timelines at handover and the incident manager reviews open cases daily through approved closure. Case histories and closure reviews are example evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: The SOC correlates central logs, endpoint alerts and network-flow records to detect credential misuse, malicious execution, unauthorized connections and suspected exfiltration. Analysts investigate anomalies, tune detections as risks change, and provide triaged alerts and recommended actions to the duty lead and system owner as needed, plus a daily summary including coverage gaps. Detection rules, sensor-health reports and investigation cases are example evidence. System owners deploy sensors and remediate gaps; Legal reviews monitoring scope and privacy constraints before onboarding or expanding collection. This is a partial/shared contribution; statement entries identify only implemented sections; all other sections remain system work.

statements.description: For onboarded assets, the SOC continuously monitors central logs, endpoint alerts and network-flow records for attacks and unauthorized connections using the configured monitoring objectives.
SOC detection rules correlate credential misuse, malicious execution and suspected exfiltration indicators against the assigned monitoring objectives; alerts become triaged investigation cases.
The SOC analyzes endpoint and network-flow telemetry for unauthorized local, network and remote connections, recording and investigating detections.
SOC analysts correlate centralized logs, endpoint detection alerts and network-flow analysis to identify unauthorized system use and record the results in cases.
SOC analysts investigate detected events and anomalies, correlate related evidence, record findings and recommend response actions in the case timeline.
The SOC duty lead adjusts monitoring intensity and detection rules when risk or credible threat information changes, recording the change and rationale.
The SOC supplies triaged alerts and recommended actions to the duty lead and system owner as needed and provides a daily summary including coverage gaps.
